subject: Post-discovery checklist: DPA notify timing, subprocessors, and residency confirmation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@evidenthealth.com>, Tom Grant <t.grant@evidenthealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: DPA points & next steps (data residency, notify window, subprocessors)

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good to meet the Evident Health team. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can map the proposal and DPA updates to your procurement checklist: 

1) Data residency: you asked about keeping inference logs in us-east-1 only. We can support region pinning for logs and model serving. Please confirm whether logs must never cross regions (some maintenance windows may route to a secondary region for short windows).

2) PII / scoped telemetry: you requested an option to avoid persisting any patient-identifiable text in logs. We have a configurable telemetry filter; outline below is what we can commit to in the addendum.

3) DPA role mapping (controller vs processor): you indicated Evident will be controller for patient data. We typically operate as processor for inference requests, but we can add clarifying language and a short schedule for subprocessors.

4) Breach / subprocessor notify: your procurement team asked for a 48-hour notify window for incidents involving PII. Our standard DPA has a 72-hour notify clause with escalation language — we can propose a 48-hour SLA for covered incidents for enterprise contracts pending legal review.

Next steps / attachments: I attached the latest DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and a simple dataflow diagram that maps what flows to Redwood logs. Can you confirm the residency requirement (strict us-east-1 vs preferred), and whether Evident requires a firm 48-hour notification commitment in the DPA?

I'll loop in our security and legal SMEs if you want a short focused call to go through the DPA redlines. Proposed times: tomorrow 9–11am PT or Friday 1–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri.yom@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (stub), redwood-dataflow-evident.png (stub)
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@evidenthealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Grant <t.grant@evidenthealth.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA points & next steps (data residency, notify window, subprocessors)

Thanks Priyom — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from procurement before we pull legal in: 

- Residency: Strict us-east-1 residency for logs only (we can allow multi-region for model binaries/updates but logs and audit trails must remain in us-east-1 and be access-controlled).

- Telemetry: We will provide a sample list of fields that must be redacted from logs. Ideally Redwood can commit to not storing raw text for any fields that match our patient identifiers (MRN, SSN, phone). A pattern-based redaction is acceptable if you can guarantee no retention of PII.

- Notify SLA: Evident's standard is 48 hours for breaches affecting PII. Can Redwood confirm whether you can meet 48 hours for incidents that involve patient data? If not, please provide your remediation timeline and the conditions for a 72 vs 48 hour determination.

Also — can you share whatever SOC2 / security artifacts you normally provide for procurement review? A summary PDF works.

We can do the focused call Friday 1–2pm PT if your security/legal folks are available.

Best,
Alice Monroe
Senior Procurement Manager, Evident Health
alice.monroe@evidenthealth.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@evidenthealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Apr 2028 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA points & next steps (data residency, notify window, subprocessors)

Hi Alice — looping in legal and security. I reviewed the DPA v3 attached and can outline the following positions we can take ahead of a formal redline: 

- Controller / Processor: We will accept the language that Evident Health is Controller and Redwood is Processor for the processing activities described. We will add explicit language clarifying limited controller responsibilities (e.g., validating lawful basis) and Redwood's subprocessor oversight process.

- Subprocessors: We maintain a subprocessor list in the DPA appendix and provide 30 days' notice for additions for enterprise customers; we can include an exceptions carve-out for urgent cloud-provider changes with post-notice. If Evident requires pre-approval for all subprocessors, please let us know — that will be a non-standard change and needs exec approval.

- Notify SLA: Redwood's standard is 72 hours for incidents that meet our incident criteria. We can commit to a 48-hour notification timeline for confirmed incidents involving PII/patient identifiers for enterprise customers if Evident is willing to accept the following: (1) notification is for confirmed incidents only (we will provide timely status updates until final), and (2) Redwood retains the right to delay public disclosure only as required by law or a controlling authority. If that aligns, I will prepare redline language for the DPA addendum.

- Telemetry / PII filtering: We can add an appended schedule to the DPA that documents a per-field redaction requirement; engineering (cc'd Aditya) will confirm whether pattern-based filters can be applied at ingestion and whether we can provide attestations to non-retention for matching PII fields.

Attachments: provisional redline placeholder will be ready after your confirmation on the residency strictness.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@evidenthealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA points & next steps (data residency, notify window, subprocessors)

Alice / team — happy to confirm the technical constraints around the asks: 

- Residency: We can enforce retention of logs in a single AWS region (us-east-1) via bucket policies and VPC endpoints. Short exceptions: system maintenance or cross-region failover for <4 hours is possible and will be explicitly called out. We will document retention and replica policies in the DPA schedule.

- PII redaction: Our ingestion pipeline supports regex / pattern-based redaction and named-field suppression. For Evident, we can implement an ingestion filter to drop configured fields before writing to long-term storage; we will retain operational telemetry (request ids, latency metrics) but can commit to dropping raw text for designated fields. We will provide a short technical attestation (SOC2 supplement) describing the filter behavior.

- Logging retention / access controls: Default audit logs are retained 90 days; we can support extended retention (e.g., 1 year) for an enterprise contract with associated cost. Access to logs will require RBAC and SSO integration with Evident's IdP; we can provide time-bound access tokens for joint investigations.

- Attachments: SOC2-summary-2027.pdf included here is a high-level artifact for procurement. If you need more detailed evidence (e.g., control mappings), we can provide them under an NDA / controlled-access portal.

If you confirm strict us-east-1 for logs and the 48-hour notify requirement as described by Lauren, we'll prepare a targeted DPA redline and a short tech appendix for your security team.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Attachments: SOC2-summary-2027.pdf (stub)
